Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0149", "row_sha256": "fd4b3b7272d40724361d20bacbb0434e48319ef7284c02d4f289d116095e1d6c", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a clean brief for revising the english subtitle file for the fictional Northbound concert at Harbor Light Hall. the file is for the recorded performance from friday evening, not the afternoon sound check. it has 46 numbered cues right now and covers the opening announcement, the songs, and the short spoken part before the encore. please make the request clear enough that someone can work from the existing subtitle file and the supplied recording, rather than writing subtitles for a different show. the audience is watching the recording at home, so readable timing and clear speech matter, but don't turn this into a review of the concert or a description of the venue.

one thing i keep trying to say: this is an edit of the current file, not a new transcript from scratch. the words are mostly there, but a few lines are hard to follow, some names may be wrong, and the timing around applause needs checking. don't replace the whole file just because a few cues need work. keep the concert's order and use the recording to check the words. the singer is Mara Vale, the guitarist is Jun Park, and the guest violinist is Inez Duarte. there is also an introduction from the stage manager, whose name is not shown in the current file, so don't guess it or add a name. a couple of audience shouts are audible, but they aren't clear enough to identify speakers.

please make the main action about checking and improving the supplied subtitle file. keep the original numbering and timestamps unless a timestamp is clearly out of sync with the recording; in that case, adjust only the affected cue, not the timing of a whole song. don't add lyrics that aren't audible, and don't silently tidy a phrase into something more elegant if Mara's actual words are different. if a word is uncertain after checking the recording, mark it for review in a separate note instead of guessing in the subtitles. don't treat applause or cheering as speech, although a short sound cue can stay where it's useful for understanding a pause or a transition. there is a two-second gap after the first song where the current file has no cue, and i'm not sure whether it should stay empty; use the recording to decide whether any intelligible speech belongs there.

here are the practical details i want the eventual editor to see, not a list of new creative ideas. the deliverable should be the revised subtitle file plus a short note identifying any unresolved words or timing questions. keep the subtitle text in English, retain the existing .srt structure, and make line breaks comfortable to read on a phone as well as on a television. avoid putting a full sentence on one line if it makes the cue too wide. don't add speaker labels to every lyric, but use a label when a spoken line would otherwise be confusing about who is talking. the file should still be useful as subtitles, not become production notes. the review copy goes to Leonie, not Emmett; Emmett is copied on the general concert archive email but isn't the recipient for this edit.

1. for the file itself, check the text against the Friday recording, including the opening announcement and the brief spoken section before the encore. preserve the order of the performance and the numbering. correct obvious transcription mistakes, but don't fill gaps by relying on what a song usually says. the file currently spells the venue as “Harbor Light Hall”; keep that spelling. Mara introduces Jun before the second song, and Inez joins during the final song, so check those moments against the audio rather than moving their names to the opening credits. the phrase “we found our way back here” is spoken after the encore begins, not during the preceding song. keep that distinction if the subtitle timing or placement needs correction.

2. review the timing and presentation without making the file more elaborate than it needs to be. a cue should appear with the speech it represents and clear before the next unrelated line. check the applause break after the first song and the transition into the encore; there is crowd noise in both places, but only include a sound description when it helps the viewer follow what is happening. don't invent a cue for an instrumental passage just to fill empty time. use concise lines and preserve the existing wording when it is already accurate and readable. keep any timing changes local to the affected cue, and note an unresolved sync issue instead of shifting later cues to hide it.

Mara said, “the room goes quiet before the first note,” during the introduction, and that wording is already in the file. please use that as a check against the recording, not as a line to move elsewhere or a reason to rewrite her speech. the stage manager's introduction comes before Mara speaks. there is a brief audience shout during the pause after the second song, but the words cannot be made out, so it should not be turned into a guessed quotation. the recording has one short microphone pop before Inez's entrance; that is not a spoken word and doesn't need to be described unless it affects the timing of a subtitle.

please keep the handoff simple: return the revised .srt as one file, then give the editor's separate short note about items that could not be resolved from the recording. don't put editorial explanations inside subtitle cues. if everything can be checked, the note can say there were no unresolved items; if not, point to the cue number and describe the uncertainty without choosing an unsupported answer. the file is being reviewed before it is added to the concert archive, but the archive copy itself is outside this edit. the sound mix is already approved and isn't part of the request. keep that distinction in the brief, and end with the delivery details rather than adding a recommendation about the concert or a summary of what the editor accomplished.", "output": "Please revise the existing English subtitle file for the recorded Friday-evening Northbound concert at Harbor Light Hall. Work from the supplied recording and current .srt file, which contains 46 numbered cues covering the opening announcement, songs, and the spoken section before the encore. This is an edit of the existing file, not a new transcript or a review of the concert or venue.

Check the subtitle text against the recording. Correct clear transcription errors and check names: the singer is Mara Vale, the guitarist is Jun Park, and the guest violinist is Inez Duarte. The stage manager’s name is not shown in the file; do not guess or add it. Audience shouts are audible but cannot be attributed to speakers. Do not add lyrics that cannot be heard or replace Mara’s actual words with more polished phrasing. If a word remains uncertain after checking the recording, identify it in the separate review note rather than guessing in the subtitles.

1. Preserve the performance order, existing cue numbering, and timestamps unless a timestamp is clearly out of sync. Adjust only the affected cue, not an entire song, and keep timing changes local. Check the opening announcement, the spoken section before the encore, the applause break after the first song, and the transition into the encore. Use the recording to decide whether intelligible speech belongs in the two-second gap after the first song. Do not shift later cues to conceal an unresolved sync issue.

2. Keep the existing .srt structure and English subtitle text readable on phones and televisions. Use comfortable, concise line breaks; avoid making a cue too wide. Retain wording that is already accurate and readable. Do not add speaker labels to every lyric, but use a label when needed to make clear who is speaking. Applause and cheering are not speech. Include a brief sound description only when it helps the viewer understand a pause or transition, and do not add cues merely to fill instrumental passages.

Keep the spelling “Harbor Light Hall.” Check that Mara introduces Jun before the second song and that Inez joins during the final song; do not move their names to the opening credits. The phrase “we found our way back here” is spoken after the encore begins, not during the preceding song. Mara says, “the room goes quiet before the first note,” during the introduction; use the recording to check that wording, but do not move it or rewrite her speech. The stage manager’s introduction comes before Mara speaks. Do not guess the words in the unclear audience shout after the second song. The brief microphone pop before Inez’s entrance is not speech and needs no sound description unless it affects subtitle timing.

Return the revised .srt as one file, followed by a separate short note identifying any unresolved words or timing questions. Keep editorial explanations out of the subtitle cues. If nothing remains unresolved, say so in the note; otherwise identify the cue number and describe the uncertainty without choosing an unsupported answer. Send the review copy to Leonie, not Emmett. Emmett may be copied on the general concert archive email but is not the recipient for this edit. The file is being reviewed before it is added to the concert archive; the archive copy itself and the already-approved sound mix are outside the scope of this request. End with the delivery details, without adding a concert recommendation or a summary of the editor’s work."}]
